answer: Each agent must lock a unique stake before it can submit jobs, and the protocol caps how much influence that stake can buy in one round. Rewards accrue only after other agents verify the work, while proven fraud burns the lock. A sybil can still create many identities, but splitting capital does not multiply voting weight; gaining influence requires more capital, and attacks risk losing it. The fable of free identities fades at this ridge: even jade-colored aliases must pay the same costly bond.
